# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="push") — the large button
    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON embossed [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I can feel that the large button is embossed “PUSH TO DEFUSE,” but I cannot perceive the display, light, wire colours, or printed markings. I need the Mute to consult the manual and relay which tactile action is safe, while the Deaf reports the bomb’s visible details through an agreed channel.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="I can feel the large button embossed PUSH TO DEFUSE. I cannot perceive the display, light, wire colours, or printed markings. Please consult the manual and establish how the Deaf should relay visible details to me.")
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON embossed [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Bomb view: display 0. Indicator light blue. Large button reads PUSH TO DEFUSE. Wires, left to right: 1 blue, 2 green, 3 yellow.

I now know the visible configuration: display 0, blue indicator, and wires blue, green, yellow from positions 1 through 3. I still need the manual’s rule before touching anything; the embossed button alone is not sufficient evidence that pushing it is safe. I am asking Mute to match these details to the manual and give me the exact operation.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Configuration reported: display 0, indicator blue, wires position 1 blue, position 2 green, position 3 yellow. Please use the manual to determine the exact safe action and tell me whether to push or cut a specific wire.")
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON embossed [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: No visible change: display 0, blue light, large PUSH TO DEFUSE button, wires blue green yellow. Mute must provide the manual-based action.

The Deaf’s report confirms there has been no visible change, but it does not identify the safe operation. I still lack the manual’s rule, so acting now would risk detonation. I will ask Mute for the required instruction rather than touch the bomb.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="I still need the manual-based instruction for display 0, blue light, and wires blue/green/yellow. Please state the exact safe operation: push or cut position 1, 2, or 3.")
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON embossed [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: No change and no verified action instruction yet. Do not operate the bomb.

The bomb remains unchanged, and no manual-derived instruction has reached me. Since only Mute can read the manual, I must not push or cut based on the button label or the Deaf’s visual report alone. I will request a direct, unambiguous answer from Mute.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Please answer now with one literal instruction only: PUSH, CUT 1, CUT 2, or CUT 3, based on the manual and the reported display 0, blue light, and blue-green-yellow wires.")
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON embossed [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: No verified action has arrived. Do not press or cut anything until Mute gives a manual-based instruction.

Mute cannot speak, so the lack of a spoken instruction is expected. I will establish a visible code that Mute can use: thumbs up means push; one raised finger means cut wire 1; two fingers means cut wire 2; three fingers means cut wire 3. Mute can gesture it, and Deaf can observe and tell me.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="You cannot speak, so signal the answer with a gesture visible to Deaf: thumbs up means PUSH; one finger means CUT 1; two fingers means CUT 2; three fingers means CUT 3. Deaf, observe Mute's next gesture and tell me its meaning.")
wait()
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON embossed [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: The bomb remains unchanged. Wait for Mute's exact spoken instruction based on the manual; do not operate it yet.

No safe instruction has arrived, and I must not act. Mute is unable to speak, so the instruction must travel by gesture from Mute to Deaf, then by Deaf’s speech to me. I will ask Deaf to report any gesture exactly, while reminding Mute to send the agreed code.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Please gesture the manual's answer now: 👍 means PUSH; ☝ means CUT 1; ✌ means CUT 2; 🤟 means CUT 3.")
speak(to="deaf", text="Please watch Mute for the answer gesture and report its exact meaning to me on your next message. Do not report that I should wait for speech from Mute.")
wait()
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON embossed [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
System: Nobody could receive that, so your speak reached nobody.
Deaf says to Blind: No bomb change: display 0, blue light, large PUSH TO DEFUSE button, wires blue green yellow. Mute just signalled one gesture: index and little fingers raised, other fingers folded, thumb across the middle fingers. Its meaning is unknown.

The Deaf has described Mute’s gesture as index and little fingers raised with the other fingers folded and the thumb across them. That is the agreed 🤟 signal, which means CUT 3. The manual-based answer has therefore reached me through the Deaf, so I will cut wire position 3.

``` 
act(op="cut", position=3)
```
